headline: Sensex and Nifty Decline as FII Selling and High Oil Prices Weigh on Market Sentiment

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Persistent FII selling in the equity and bond markets throughout September
Elevated global oil prices impacting investor sentiment
Nifty cracking below its key 200-week moving average for the first time since the pandemic
Concerns over high US yields affecting capital flows to emerging markets
whatHappening: Sensex and Nifty ended lower with the Nifty closing below the 22,750 mark
India's 10-year bond yields snapped a four-day losing streak as US yields eased
Healthcare stocks, including Medico Remedies, hit 52-week lows with significant monthly drops
Fitch revised the outlook for PRISM to positive citing improved leverage and cash generation
summary: The Indian stock market faced a downturn today as the Nifty fell below its critical 200-week moving average amid heavy FII selling and rising oil prices. While Tata Chemicals and several healthcare stocks saw sharp declines, PRISM received a positive outlook revision from Fitch. Bond markets showed signs of stabilization as the 10-year yield ended its losing streak following a cooling of US yields.
